My wife took a photo of our iron to sell it online — and its reflection turned into an alien holding a phone

I've been through fire, water, and everything in between — nothing scares me anymore. Except walking past my building's entrance, where the neighborhood grannies sit on the bench like a tribunal. That path should really be called the road to absolution.

Nobody ever forced me to go to school. I'd oversleep, and my dad would be thrilled — grab a shovel, a pitchfork, go muck out the barn. But hey, at least no homework! Same story the next day. By the third day, before my dad even opened his eyes, I was already dressed, backpack on, tying my shoes by the door. That's how I fell in love with school.
Stop making me mad, or I'll put your number in an ad: "Will dig your garden for free — just say thanks!"
The doctor hooks him up for an ECG: "Let's see what your heart is missing." The heartbeat line on the printout spells out one word: "money."
A big girl grabs a guy's cheek and asks, "Got a girlfriend?" He stammers, "No." She squeezes harder, leaving his cheek bright red: "You do now."

They say before you do anything, you should filter it through four sieves: the sieve of truth - is it actually true? The sieve of kindness - will it do any good? The sieve of usefulness - does it even make sense? And the sieve of health - will it wreck your back? But in the end, everything gets decided by the real final sieve: the sieve of laziness. Can I even be bothered to do this?
In America: "Let's go to the dealership and pick out your first car." Here: "There's a Lada in the garage — grandpa drove it, I drove it, now it's yours." Just build it back together first.

A guy asks his girlfriend on the couch, "Why don't you ever want to go out with me?" Then he remembers: at the bar it was "I'm tired, let's go home," camping it was "I'm cold, there are bugs, let's go home," at the movies it was "This film's boring, let's leave," and at the party it was "I don't like it here, let's go home."
If someone tells you "love doesn't exist," don't believe them. That person had it, and it was real. Someone just broke their heart so badly they still haven't recovered
Looks like the makeup had a mind of its own today.
"Sonya, I heard you're on a diet? How much have you lost?" "Five kilos." "And how much did you weigh total?" "A hundred and fifty." "Ah, well that's like a bolt falling off a tank."
As a kid: "Mom, why do I need jeans, it's only -16 out!" Now: I wrap myself in fuzzy leggings the second it hits +7.

"Lena, why did you put on such fancy lingerie? You're only going to the dentist!"
"What if he's a bit cheeky?"

A professor notices that one student at the seminar is clearly tipsy and says:
"Young man, you're drunk! Leave the lecture hall immediately!"
"Professor, come on, I'm completely sober!"
"Sober, huh? Then write out the formula for the Laplacian in toroidal coordinates."
The student walks up and confidently fills the whole board with a long formula. The professor checks it against a reference book for ages and finally admits:
"Impressive. I couldn't remember that formula sober either."
The student shrugs:
"Well, sober, neither could I!"
Selling rollerblades, brand new, never used... turned out the size didn't fit.

An old man is sitting on a bench, crying his eyes out. A guy walks by and asks, "What's wrong, old timer?" The old man sniffles, "Well, I just got married." "Ah, I get it — she's old and cranky?" "No way, she's gorgeous, thirty years younger than me!" "So she's got a nasty temper, or can't cook?" "Not at all, she's an angel — cooks, cleans, does laundry, amazing in bed..." "Then why on earth are you crying, you should be celebrating!" "Because... I forgot the way home."
If I ever became a painter, here's my masterpiece: set up the easel, grab the brush... and just write the word "MOUNTAIN" on the canvas. Why draw it when you can just label it?
Guys in their thirties in skinny jeans basically look like this: matchstick legs holding up everything else — total heron energy.

"Gonna hit me?"
"No, gonna wipe you!"
Why waste money on a barber when you can just cut your hair at home? Here's how that actually turns out:
Grandmas on a park bench swapping phone numbers of scammers they'd trust with their life savings.

"How do you manage to constantly fight with your wife but still get along great with your mother-in-law?"
"Easy — back in the day, she was the one who was dead set against our wedding!"
Special delivery: bringing the latest news straight to the next village
A fisherman in a face mask can't figure out why the fish won't bite. Turns out the fish is wearing a mask too — social distancing, apparently!
I bet the first person to ever try moldy cheese was some grandpa from a family of cheesemakers! And it probably came with the words: "Are you crazy, throwing that out? It's delicious, eat it all!"
Love is waking up early just to watch her sleep.
Ugh, there's absolutely nothing to watch, so boring... Meanwhile my cat is just sitting there staring at the wall like: wow, this is gorgeous!

Medical school, the first lecture of spring. The professor walks in: "Ah, spring... boys checking out girls, girls checking out boys. Reminds me of my youth — a buddy and I went to a club, and we both liked the same girl. She picked him, not me, and left with him. So I was left out in the cold." Pause. "And my friend — without his nose. Write down today's topic: 'Syphilis and its consequences.'"

The wife says: "Honey, tomorrow's our wedding anniversary, should we slaughter a piglet?" The husband replies: "The piglet didn't do anything. We should slaughter Steve — he's the one who introduced us."
A truly good conversation partner doesn't just listen closely — they also top off your glass right on time.
Eat whatever you want and stop torturing yourself over it. You only live once. And if someone starts lecturing you about your weight, just eat their lecture too.
Went to the store just for a loaf of bread, and I'm walking home with two bags of who-knows-what worth $50. Oh, and of course I forgot the bread.
You know what men are true masters of? One thing they're absolute champions at — ruining a woman's mood out of nowhere!

Some friends of mine have an African grey parrot living with their Doberman. The parrot learned to imitate the doorbell — the dog instantly starts barking like crazy, and the parrot yells right back in the owner's voice: "Waldan, down!" How that dog hasn't lost its mind yet is a real mystery.
A patient tells the doctor, "Doc, I broke my arm in three different places!" The doctor replies, "Well, then just stop going to those places."
A husband stuck a note on his wife's fuel cap: "Olya, remember, you're on diesel." Olya fired back in the comments: "Don't take me for an idiot, I drive a Hyundai, not a diesel!"
The main thing after getting up from the stool: don't forget, out of habit, to pull your underwear back up...
A month ago my cat went missing. A week later I found a cat and brought it home. Today my actual cat came back. Now I have two identical cats.
A boring round hole? Not for this guy — he carved a flower-shaped opening just to fit the pipe through. That's dedication... to doing it wrong.
This is basically how my friendship with skiing always ends.
Go like that guy for me, my hands are kind of tied right now.
"How's life?" "All good, right on track." The track:

My friend's cat once got hurt, and while it was being treated, everyone fussed over it non-stop: petting it, feeding it treats, propping up soft pillows. It fully recovered. But a couple weeks later, it suddenly collapsed again. My friend panicked and rushed it to the vet. He examined the cat, came out and said, "There's nothing I can do." She nearly fainted, stammering, "What's wrong with her?!" The vet replied, "She's faking it."
When the hotel listing says "just a 5-minute walk to the beach," but this is what it actually looks like.
Ugh, the tire's flat... Completely?! No, just on the bottom.
Made dumplings and they turned into some weird tower spilling out of the pot. But when you're really hungry, it'll do just fine.

A friend of mine who lives in a dorm was given a black kitten. She got home late at night, her parents were already asleep, and her mom answered the door. Her dad, lying in bed, hears the door creak and his daughter's voice: "Mom, meet Robert!" His mind went straight to the worst, and he jumped up to get dressed in a hurry. Five minutes later, while mom and daughter were calmly having tea in the kitchen gushing about how handsome Robert was, dad showed up in the doorway beaming, fully dressed in a suit and tie, holding a chilled bottle of moonshine...
Went to grab my jeans, and two little eyes were staring back at me from inside the pant legs — turns out the cat had moved in.
Remote gym class: the teacher turns on the camera, and the kid is already hanging upside down under the desk while the laptop dutifully shows him "present" on the call.
Standing at a scenic overlook, taking in the view, when it suddenly hits me: today was definitely not the day to pick these pants.
The most important thing after a rough night — don't spot someone doing a handstand on the bars: hungover, it genuinely looks like they have no head at all.

A notice pinned in the stairwell: "Dear neighbors, don't fall for the cat Busya's act! Even if she collapses in the hallway and starts wailing like she's starving — don't believe her. At home she gets premium food and a soft couch, she's just naturally skinny. Don't give in to her provocations, it's embarrassing for us. Busya isn't homeless, she has a fully furnished apartment — she's just a world-class con artist!"

One night hunger struck, so I decided to sneak into the kitchen for food. The house was dark, so I figured everyone was asleep. I tiptoed through the dining room, quietly opened the fridge, and poured milk over my cereal without a sound. Funny thing is, it was only seven in the evening — everything looked dark because I was wearing sunglasses. Meanwhile my parents were sitting right there eating dinner, watching me creep across the kitchen and pour milk into my cereal.

I dozed off on the bus and woke up convinced I'd missed my stop. Screamed "Help!" and bolted out the front door. Stepped outside — realized I was wrong and still had a long way to go. So I hopped back in through the back door and sat right back down in my seat. It got so quiet on that bus the driver even turned off the music.

Yesterday I was standing in line at the supermarket checkout, and there was a man with his son. The boy finished his juice box, and the dad took the empty carton from him, smoothed it out neatly, and said, "We still need to pay for this one." The kid was baffled: "Why? I already drank it all!" The dad sighed and explained, "That's how it works, son. It's called credit."

A guy tells the doctor, "Doc, my dog got sick!" The doctor scribbles something on the chart — his handwriting is so bad the patient can't make out a single word. He glances at the note and just says, "Hello there!"
This is what a plumbing company's van looks like — from the side it seems like the guy is driving while sitting on a toilet.

Life stages have their own rules: as a kid you do it while they let you, as a teen while you don't get caught, in your youth while it's still fun, in adulthood while you still can, and in old age while you still remember why you started.

I don't have Facebook or Instagram, so I make friends the old-fashioned way: every day I go outside and tell random strangers what I ate, how I'm feeling, what I did last night, and what I'm doing tomorrow. I show them photos of my friends and my hamster, pictures of me fixing my bike, and baby photos from when I was two. I eavesdrop on other people's conversations and chime in with "Like!" And guess what — it's working! As of today I've got five followers: two cops, a psychiatrist, a psychologist, and a male nurse.

A third-grader's essay on "What is a Grandma?": "A grandma is a woman who has no small kids of her own, but she loves other people's. A grandpa is just a grandma who's a man — he takes boys for walks and talks about fishing. Grandmas don't have to do anything except come visit. They can't run because they're old, but they always have enough money for the carousel. On walks they stop to admire a pretty leaf or a caterpillar, and they never say 'Hurry up.' They wear glasses and can take their teeth out. A grandma doesn't need to be smart, she just has to answer questions like 'Why do dogs chase cats?' or 'Where's a worm's head?' When they read you a book, they never skip a page or say you've already heard this one. Everyone should get a grandma, because they're the only grown-ups with free time for kids."

I told the kindergarten my son won't touch anything with cottage cheese — no casserole, no cheese pancakes. This morning the teacher sends me a video of him happily eating... casserole. I ask how she pulled it off. She says: we don't have casserole here, only cottage cheese cake!

The most exhausting part of adulting is that it never stops. There's always some new mess to deal with. If you're feeling relaxed, it just means you've ignored a million things you're supposed to be doing. Blow off a million tasks today, and tomorrow you've got two million.

I asked my husband to post an ad to find a mate for our male guinea pig, then left for work. That evening a friend called, laughing so hard she couldn't get a word out. She sent me a screenshot of the ad: "Wild male guinea-pig terrier is feeling down right now and seeks comfort in the arms of a fluffy redheaded mermaid. Fresh carrots included, plus a wheel of mad passion. All inquiries go through the owner, aka Master."

Whenever I start feeling guilty about barely seeing my relatives, I remember this one story. Two women are riding a bus, and one keeps staring at the other, until she finally works up the courage to ask:
"Sorry, have we met before? Your face looks so familiar..."
"Well, I'm your cousin."

China officially has no pension fund — yet everyone still gets a pension. Turns out the trick is simple: a chunk of your salary gets set aside into an account with your name on it. You just can't touch it early. Once you hit retirement age, you get access to your own savings. So there really is no pension fund — you were your own pension fund all along. And if you don't make it to retirement, your heirs inherit the account.

An curious traveler once visited an old master.
"Master, is it true you can lie on a bed of nails?"
"Sure, I suppose," the master said, a bit puzzled.
"Show me, show me!" the visitor begged.
The master shrugged, dumped a couple of boxes of nails on the floor, threw a mattress on top, and calmly lay down.
"No, that's all wrong!" the traveler protested. "You're supposed to hammer the nails into a board, points up, and lie on those!"
"Are you an idiot?" the master asked politely.

A friend told me about her super tidy cat — they'd trained him to use the toilet and even flush after himself, adjusting the button so it'd press easily. One day she noticed he'd been in the bathroom forever, went to check, and there he was: for half an hour straight he'd been pressing the flush, listening to the water, and pressing it again. That day the whole building ran out of cold water.

Watermelons really need to sort themselves out with those seeds scattered all over the fruit. They could take a page from the melon's book and bunch them all in one spot, so you could just scoop them out with a spoon and eat in peace. Now that would be service.

Took the kids to a local farm once, and we found a little goat with its horns stuck in the fence, sitting in the grass looking absolutely miserable. We tried to free it but it was really wedged in there. Pet the poor thing, fed it grass through the wire, then ran to the ticket booth to report an animal in distress. Before I even finished saying "there's a goat stuck..." the guy just waved his hand tiredly: "Yeah, we know. That's Brenda. She can get out whenever she wants. She just loves the attention."
Damn drama-queen goat.
Australians believe meeting a black cat brings good luck — because a cat is the safest thing you could possibly run into in Australia.

Outside the bakery, an eighty-something grandma in a zebra-print dress, huge earrings, and bright red nails is yelling into her phone: "Vera, why are you being difficult? The grandkids will get you on the train, you'll rattle around a bit, and in the morning we'll switch you into a taxi and drop you off. What do you mean 'wrong age'? You won't even have to stand up — they just pick you up, carry you, set you down, pick you up again. Hand to hand, and boom, you're there. All you have to do is lie there, sip champagne, and occasionally signal you're alive and want a refill."

We left Friday for our beloved country house, and came back Sunday from that damn vegetable patch barely alive. Meanwhile the cat, perched right on her shoulder, cheers her on: "Come on, Natasha, work ennobles a person!"

Yesterday I got fired from a job I loved, because of people I loved. So here's a reminder for everyone: they'll toss you out the second they decide you're not needed anymore. Stop staying late. Stop checking work email on weekends. A job is supposed to fund your life, not become your entire life.

I'm unemployed. Out of pure spite I wrote a resume like: "I'm a gloomy jerk who wants to work less and get paid more, and I don't care what you think of me" — then sent it out everywhere. Yesterday, out of nowhere, I got invited to an interview. Now I'm sitting here nervous — I want to go, but I'm terrified because I have no idea why they'd actually want me.

A friend's wife found a bald spot on their cat's belly and panicked, thinking it was ringworm. She rushed to the vet — turns out it was just his belly button. My wife and I went looking on our own cats too: pink and round, right in the middle of the belly. I told my coworkers, and now "find the cat's belly button" has spread through the office like an epidemic. Fair warning: whoever tries it gets bitten and kicked by the hind legs.

"Citizen! Come here!" "And who are you?" "Security officer!" "Then identify yourself and show your papers." "I'm not obligated to show anything!" "Well then, I'm a security officer too!" "Show your papers!" "And I'm not obligated either!"

I set my alarm to ocean waves, imagining a gentle wake-up by the sea, and cranked the volume all the way up. Turns out the waves only lasted the first ten seconds — then a massive ship horn blasted through. I somehow fell out of both sides of the bed at once, the cat leapt in terror, smacked its head on the ironing board, which toppled over and dropped the iron right on my foot. Well, at least I'm wide awake now.

A wife tells her husband: "Look what a lovely couple our new neighbors are! He hugs her, kisses her, whispers sweet nothings... why don't you ever do that with me?" The husband replies: "Honestly, I've never even met that woman before!"

They invented résumés just so people could suffer in advance. All I really want is to get wrapped up like a baby on some cold, rainy night and left right at the office door — so the employer finds me in the morning. After that, a flock of veteran secretaries will take me under their wing, a wise old turtle from accounting will spill the secrets of getting paid under the table, and a couple of friendly HR reps will teach me to fit in and survive on scraps for the first few weeks. The only one I'll ever have to watch out for is the shark from sales.

The boss is annoyed that he pays one worker more than the other, so he decides to find out why. He sends a servant to check on a broken-down cart up on the hill. The first one comes back and just says, "the wheel broke." The second one actually finds out everything: the cart's owner was hauling grain to sell at two rubles a kilo, but since the wheel's busted, he'll let it go for one ruble a kilo if someone helps fix it — and he's already lined up the blacksmith. Good deal, just needs the boss's yes. That's the whole secret behind who gets paid more.

A couple earning a combined $4,000 a month says: "At least we can afford the dentist without saving up, travel once in a while, treat ourselves without going overboard. But a house and a car are out of reach, and if we had kids we'd be broke." A couple earning $1,000: mortgage, car, two kids. The second couple just doesn't bother with their teeth.

How do you teach kids good behavior? Tarzan's been walking around naked his whole life... Cinderella strolls home well past midnight... Batman races through the city at 450 km/h... and Snow White sleeps with seven guys at once — the horror! And don't even get me started on the hedgehog, forever lost in the fog...
An engineer's wife is never at a loss — resourcefulness runs in the family.

Husband: "Why did so much money come off my card?" Wife: "I went to the store, stop yelling..." He checks the receipt: "Sausages... tangerines... bread... all fine... wait, WHAT is THIS?!" Wife: "I'm sorry..." Husband: "Why didn't you bring your own bag?!"
Two notes in the school diary. First one: "Please buy some modeling clay." A couple of weeks later: "Throws modeling clay during class."

We looked it up over lunch and found out a cat's heel is officially called the "hock joint." Okay, so what's the scientific name for "twitchy tail nerve" and "fluffy belly gland"? And what about the "purr gland"? While you're at it, find the term for the "mischief vein" — cats clearly have one.
She whispers, embarrassed: "I can't with him watching." He waves it off: "Relax, it's just the cat." Meanwhile the cat is behind the camera yelling: "More passion, guys!"
You can't hide a good mood — even her dress is smiling about it!
My wife sings around the house. Meanwhile I'm sitting outside on the bench — better the neighbors think I'm just relaxing than that I'm beating her.

"I was such a fool when I was young..."
"Well, you still look pretty young for your age!"
I wanted to surprise my husband, so I put on a schoolgirl outfit and waited for him to get home. He walks in, looks at me all grumpy, and says: "Go do your homework... I'm going to bed."
The baby's ready to climb over the seat to a total stranger just to escape hangry mom — you're not you when you're hungry!
I took this photo in front of my wife and she got mad at me. Someone explain what I did wrong — it's not every day you see a dog driving a car!
My daughter peeked into the pot and asked, "Dad, why are you boiling that ice-age squirrel?" It took me a solid minute to get what she meant.
